hz10_houthis.topic: Houthis: origins, Saada wars, Sanaa 2014, Saudi-led war and US support, Iran's arms and the proxy question

claims.text: Believing Youth (al-Shabab al-Mumin) founded in Saada in 1992 (per Hassan Zaid); the 'war' officially began 18 June 2004; Hussein al-Houthi killed September 2004, succeeded by brother Abdul-Malik; by 2008 the fifth round; hundreds killed, thousands displaced, ~3,000 arrests reported by local rights groups

Hussein al-Houthi, son of Zaidi scholar, MP 1993-97; killed shortly after 2004 fighting began; Houthis and Saleh regime fought 'a series of six intermittent wars' 2004-2010; Ansar Allah = 'Supporters of God'; Believing Youth members chanted 'Death to America, Death to Israel'
Hussein al-Houthi died 10 September 2004 in Marran, Saada; MP 1993-97 for al-Haqq; father Badreddin a Zaydi cleric who briefly led the movement
Slogan (Sarkha): 'God is great, Death to America, Death to Israel, Curse on the Jews, Victory to Islam', first chanted January 2002 at Marran
21 September 2014: Houthi fighters occupied PM's compound, army command, state TV in Sanaa; PM Basindwa resigned; UN-brokered deal signed; 100+ died in four days of clashes

CFR: Ansar Allah rooted in Zaidism (about a third of Yemen's ~34m); militarized late 2000s; overthrew government 2014; rules about a third of territory and two-thirds of population; most experts agree Iran was supplying weapons by 2014; July 2025 seizure of 750 tons of Iranian munitions; many experts call Houthis Iran's 'informal partner' rather than a classic proxy; Rough Rider struck 800+ targets per US military

CRS: Saudi-led coalition began operations March 2015; US announced 25 March 2015 'logistical and intelligence support'; later refueling, weapons transfers, intelligence, training via joint planning cell; Mattis announced 9 Nov 2018 end of US in-flight refueling; Congress passed S.J.Res.7 (Senate 54-46, House 247-175 on 4 April 2019); Trump vetoed 16 April 2019; override failed 53-45 on 2 May 2019; May 2019 emergency sales >$8bn
US midair refuelling support ended 10 Nov 2018; Mattis: US support 'not unconditional'
UNDP projected ~377,000 deaths by end-2021, ~60% indirect (hunger, disease)

UN Panel S/2024/731: 'without foreign support, the entity does not have the capacity to develop and produce complex weapon systems'; 53 items with strong similarities to Iranian materiel; Quds Force general reportedly predominant advisory role; Iran told Panel some markings did not match its production; Hizbullah 'one of the most important supporters of the Houthis'; senior Houthi official: Galaxy Leader decision 'made by the Houthi leaders'; at least 134 attacks 15 Nov 2023-31 Jul 2024, at least four seafarers killed; Houthis 'indiscriminately targeting vessels'
UN Panel S/2020/70 (Jan 2020): unlicensed engine copies, Quds-1 with Farsi label tested at Iranian facility Feb 2019; seized Iranian-made missiles
Harmouch/Jahanbani: Houthis are 'strategic allies' rather than 'mere proxies'; Hezbollah 'retains autonomy' in domestic politics
Norman Roule (ex-CIA): Iran 'seeks the product of militia actions, not the process of controlling them'; Hezbollah closest, Houthis most distant
CRS IF12587: Iran increased support to Houthis since 2014-15 incl. ballistic and cruise missiles and drones; US airstrikes began 11 January 2024; KH, Nujaba, AAH are US-designated FTOs

hz10_redsea.topic: The Red Sea campaign 2023-2026, US/UK and Israeli strikes, Rough Rider, the Oman truce, 2026 status

claims.text: Austin announced Operation Prosperity Guardian 18 Dec 2023 'to jointly address security challenges in the southern Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden'; named UK, Bahrain, Canada, France, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Seychelles, Spain; by then 100+ attacks targeting 10 merchant vessels
Biden: US and UK struck Houthi targets 12 Jan 2024 (local) in response to shipping attacks; support from Australia, Bahrain, Canada, Netherlands; 'will not hesitate'

Reuters factbox 10 July 2025: 100+ merchant ships targeted since Nov 2023; four sunk (Rubymar 2 Mar 2024, Tutor June 2024, Magic Seas 6 July 2025, Eternity C 9 July 2025), one seized, at least eight sailors killed; True Confidence March 2024 three killed; Eternity C four killed, 11 missing; Galaxy Leader crew of 25 freed January 2025
19 July 2024 Houthi drone killed one in Tel Aviv; Israel struck Hodeidah 20 July 2024; Houthi ministry 80 wounded; Gallant: Houthis attacked Israel 200+ times
Ras Isa strike 17 April 2025: at least 74 killed, 171 injured per Houthi-run health ministry (not independently verified); CENTCOM: aim 'to degrade the economic source of power of the Houthis'

Airwars: at least 224 civilians allegedly killed by US strikes in Rough Rider (Mar-6 May 2025), vs 258 in Nov 2002-Jan 2025; Ras Isa at least 84, Saada detention centre at least 68; CENTCOM no public determinations

NBC: Rough Rider began 15 March 2025; cost more than $1bn; ~2,000 bombs and missiles incl. 75+ Tomahawks; seven drones shot down; two fighter jets lost at sea; munitions cost disputed ($775m vs ~$400m)

Amnesty: 28 April 2025 US strike on Saada migrant detention centre; Houthi authorities: 117 detained, 61 killed, 56 injured; Amnesty: indiscriminate, no evidence of military objective; CENTCOM 'assessing all reports of civilian harm'
6 May 2025: Trump said Houthis 'capitulated'; Oman FM: 'neither side will target the other'; State Dept: deal did not cover Israel-Houthi conflict; Houthi official: operations remain support for Gaza
Netanyahu after US-Houthi truce: Israel 'will defend itself by itself'; Israeli officials said no advance notice

Israeli strike on Sanaa (28 Aug 2025) killed Houthi PM Ahmed al-Rahawi and several ministers; 24 Aug 2025 strikes killed 10 per health officials; Israeli military: 'a Houthi terrorist regime military target'; al-Mashat vowed vengeance

CRS July 2026: shipping attacks Oct 2023-Dec 2024, paused early 2025; resumed on some non-US ships July 2025; suspended attacks on Israel after Oct 2025 Gaza ceasefire; restarted during 2026 Iran war; July 2026 announced targeting of Saudi-linked ships; uneasy truce since 2022
Houthis entered the Iran war 28 March 2026 with ballistic missiles at southern Israel; Saree: attacks target only 'the Israeli and American enemy'
2026 Houthi launches at Israel 28 Mar-9 Jun 2026 intercepted or fell in open areas; no injuries recorded; attacks paused after Iran-war ceasefire (April), resumed briefly June 2026

20 July 2026 Houthis declared maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia ('siege for a siege'); attacks on Saudi tankers; 25 July Aramco suspended Jazan refinery; 27 July Abqaiq hit — Riyadh blamed Iran-backed Iraqi militias, Houthis claimed it; 30 July Saudi Red Sea coalition with 13 countries

CTP-ISW 26 Sept 2026: Houthi and government forces fighting at Jabal Naman near Bab al-Mandab; Saudi/government strikes on Houthi stockpiles; Houthi missile/drone attacks on Saudi Arabia continue; Iraq and Lebanon 'nothing significant to report'

AFP 3 Oct 2026: 80 combatants killed in a day near Taiz; 2022 truce held until fighting resumed in July 2026; Houthis say 1,350 Saudi strikes since; WFP: nearly three-quarters of Yemenis cannot meet basic food needs
27 Sept 2026: Houthis said Saudi raids on a Taiz market killed or wounded nearly 50 (Houthi figures, unverified)

hz10_iraq.topic: Iraqi militias: PMF, Kataib Hezbollah, the 2019-20 escalation and Soleimani, Tower 22, 2026

claims.text: Late Dec 2019 rocket attack on an Iraqi base killed a US contractor (27 Dec per Esper); US blamed Kataib Hezbollah; US strikes (29 Dec) killed 25 KH fighters; Iran-backed militias attacked US embassy in Baghdad, ending 1 Jan; Trump ordered ~750 troops deployed; Pentagon: Soleimani 'was actively developing plans to attack American diplomats and service members'; strike 'aimed at deterring future Iranian attack plans'

Soleimani headed the Quds Force from 1998; drone strike on PMF convoy at Baghdad airport killed Soleimani and PMF deputy Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis; Pentagon called it 'decisive defensive action'; Khamenei warned of 'harsh retaliation'; NYT: no congressional approval, unclear if Iraq consulted
Airwars CI879: 3 Jan 2020, 11-13 military actors and 0-1 civilians reported killed
Tower 22, northeastern Jordan, 28 Jan 2024: Sgt William Jerome Rivers, Spc Kennedy Ladon Sanders (24), Spc Breonna Alexsondria Moffett killed; Biden blamed Iran-backed militia groups

Farida: Iraqi militias emerged after 2003; PMF established 2014 against ISIS; 'more than 160' attacks on US forces since 7 Oct 2023; Islamic Resistance in Iraq is umbrella incl. KH; US blamed KH for Jordan attack; KH said it was 'halting' operations under pressure from Iran and Iraq; Iran denies ordering attacks and says factions act independently

hz10_syria.topic: Syria in Iran's network; Israel's strikes 2013-2019; Israel's aid and arms to Golan rebels 2013-18; post-Assad buffer zone, Sweida, talks and Sufa 53 to Oct 2026; PIJ

claims.text: Iran provided billions of dollars in aid to Assad, thousands of advisers and troops, and mobilised tens of thousands of foreign Shia fighters; Syria was the main conduit for Iranian arms to Hezbollah for four decades
Iran's foreign ministry (2 Dec 2024): Iran entered Syria 'at the official invitation of the Syrian government' and advisers stay per Damascus's wishes
Netanyahu, cabinet 13 Jan 2019: 'the IDF has attacked hundreds of times Iranian and Hezbollah targets'

Eisenkot to Sunday Times, Jan 2019: strikes on Iranian infrastructure began Jan 2017; ~2,000 bombs on Iranian targets in 2018; 'thousands of attacks without taking responsibility'; Iranian plan for ~100,000 Shia fighters (Israeli intelligence claim)
Eisenkot acknowledged Israel gave light weapons to Golan rebel groups 'for self-defense', first official acknowledgement; ToI notes raid counts in his interviews ranged 200-400
IDF: over 4,900 Syrians incl. 1,300 children treated in Israel since 2013, ~7,000 at border clinic; Operation Good Neighbor launched 2016, closed Sept 2018 after regime retook the south
WSJ June 2017 (per Jewish News): Israel gave Golan rebels cash, food, fuel, medical supplies; money paid salaries and bought arms; Fursan al-Joulan main partner; IDF neither confirmed nor denied

Foreign Policy Sept 2018: Israel armed and funded at least 12 groups 2013-July 2018, rifles, machine guns, mortars, vehicles, ~$75/month per fighter; aim to keep Iran-backed and IS fighters from border; Israeli embassy declined comment
8 Dec 2024 Netanyahu: 1974 agreement 'has collapsed'; ordered seizure of buffer zone and nearby commanding positions
IDF: ~480 strikes in 48 hours after Assad's fall; navy hit two facilities with 15 vessels; Sa'ar: to keep weapons from 'extremists'; Hermon captured; Danon: 'deployed temporarily'
UNDOF: Israel in 'violation of the 1974 disengagement agreement'; Guterres 'deeply concerned', agreement 'remains in force', calls for withdrawal
Katz 28 Jan 2025: IDF to stay on Hermon and in security zone indefinitely
16 July 2025 Israel struck Syrian defence ministry and near presidential palace; Netanyahu 'acting to save our Druze brothers'; SOHR ~260 killed in Sweida; Syria condemned
6 Jan 2026 Paris: US-supervised Israel-Syria communication cell for de-escalation agreed; no commitment to stop strikes
June 2026: Katz quoted 'we will not withdraw from the security zone in Syria'
23 Aug 2026 Jordan meeting; Syria's priority: Israeli return to pre-8 Dec 2024 lines; Golan status premature
23 Sept 2026 al-Sharaa: talks reached 'almost 90%' before Israel pulled back (his claim)
4 Oct 2026 Israel resumed Sufa 53 fortified line in Quneitra buffer zone (begun 2022); Israel: to prevent attacks by Iran-backed groups; Syria: 'flagrant breach'; Jordan and Qatar condemned
PIJ founded in Gaza 1981 by Shaqaqi and Awda; main funding Iran (Australia); US FTO 8 Oct 1997, 'receives financial assistance and training primarily from Iran'

claims.text: CRS R45046: October 2016 Saudi strike on a Sanaa funeral hall killed 140; Obama administration held a precision-guided munitions sale and limited intelligence sharing but kept refuelling; Senate passed S.J.Res.7 54-46 in March 2019; 24 May 2019 emergency sales >$8bn; Senate adopted all 22 resolutions of disapproval; three (S.J.Res. 36-38) passed both chambers and were vetoed.

Airwars: during Rough Rider it documented more incidents with higher casualties per strike than in any other US campaign; the two deadliest civilian-harm incidents in US operations in Yemen; Ras Isa at least 84 killed, 150 injured.
NBC (May 2025): two US officials, >$1bn; ~2,000 munitions worth >$775m; at least 75 Tomahawks; seven drones shot down; two fighter jets lost; a DoD official said munitions cost closer to $400m.
Amnesty 29 Oct 2025: Houthi authorities said 117 migrants detained, 61 killed, 56 injured; Amnesty found no evidence of a military objective; CENTCOM 'assessing all reports of civilian harm'.

Reuters factbox: Rubymar struck Feb 2024, sank 2 Mar 2024; True Confidence March 2024 three killed; Tutor sank June 2024, one crew never found; Magic Seas sank 6 Jul 2025; Eternity C sank 9 Jul 2025, four killed, 11 missing.

CRS July 2026: Houthis attributed strikes on Sanaa airport (after flights from Iran) to Saudi Arabia, then announced targeting of Saudi-linked ships; Oman-brokered deal: Houthis cease targeting US vessels, US halts strikes.

AFP 3 Oct 2026: 80 combatants killed over a day around Taiz per both sides (Houthi: 55+ opponents; government: 26 troops); civil war dormant after 2022 truce 'roared back to life in July'; Houthis: 94 Saudi strikes in 24h, 1,350 total.

UN Panel S/2024/731: Abdulmalik al-Houthi confirmed in June 2024 coordinating military activities with the 'so-called Islamic Resistance in Iraq' (para 12); joint operational centres in Iraq and Lebanon; 134+ attacks 15 Nov 2023-31 Jul 2024 (para 54); Hazam al-Assad: Galaxy Leader decision 'made by the Houthi leaders' (para 56); 53 items (para 70); Gen. Abdulreza Shahlai advisory role (para 72).
CFR: some experts date Iranian military support to 2009, during the Houthis' first war with the government; most agree weapons flowing by 2014.
Farida: after ISIS's military defeat in 2019 the PMF 'shifted their attention back to US targets in Iraq'.
USIP: Iran mobilized tens of thousands of foreign Shiite fighters 'from as far away as Afghanistan and Pakistan'; Pezeshkian 8 Dec 2024 statement; Khamenei 11 Dec 2024 'joint American-Zionist plot'.

Enab Baladi: Sufa 53 features an eight-metre military road, five-metre earthen berms, trenches and observation posts; Syria's foreign ministry: 'flagrant breach'; Jordan and Qatar condemned. Anadolu: Israel says it is 'designed to prevent possible attacks by Iran-backed armed groups'; begun mid-2022 near Hadr.
Rudaw: KH members and supporters stormed the US embassy, 'breaching the reception area and setting parts of the compound on fire'.
